analysis.investment_thesis: Capri Global Capital is a fast-growing NBFC compounding revenue at 37.2% and net profit at 30.4% over nine years, serving the chronically underserved MSME and affordable home loan market in India — a segment with one of the largest unmet credit demand pools in the world. At a Forward P/E of just 12.96x against FY25 profit growth of 72% (₹479 Cr vs ₹279 Cr), the PEG is approximately 0.29 — one of the most attractive growth-to-price combinations I can find.
key_strengths: Revenue has grown 17x in 9 years (₹189 Cr → ₹3,248 Cr) with consistent profit compounding at 30%+ CAGR — this is a genuine fast grower with sustained execution
Total assets doubled in 2 years from ₹15,150 Cr (FY24) to ₹24,413 Cr (FY25), signaling AUM acceleration driven by gold loans and construction finance alongside the core MSME book
Strong institutional confidence: DII holding of 20.09% alongside promoter's 59.92% stake signals alignment and credibility; QIPs in FY23 and FY25 funded growth without excessive dilution
key_risks: Finance costs are growing at 67.9% CAGR — faster than revenue at 37.2% — which means the cost of borrowed funds is compressing net interest margins and could erode profitability if interest rates remain elevated
Debt/Equity of 2.52 is high even for an NBFC; total debt of ₹15,577 Cr against equity of ₹6,673 Cr means any credit market disruption or ratings downgrade could trigger a funding squeeze
Net profit was completely flat from FY22 to FY23 (₹205 Cr both years) — the FY24-25 acceleration needs to be sustained across a full credit cycle to validate the growth narrative
red_flags: Operating cash flow has been negative every single year for 5 consecutive years (cumulative outflow ~₹12,678 Cr) — normal for a rapidly scaling lender but leaves no internal capital generation buffer during a liquidity crunch

Gold loan and construction finance are cyclically sensitive segments; aggressive expansion into these in FY24-25 creates concentration risk in segments that can deteriorate quickly in a stressed macro environment
analysis.detailed_analysis:
India's formal credit-to-GDP ratio is still well below developed markets, and MSMEs represent the most underserved segment of that gap — which is precisely the hunting ground Capri Global has staked out. The business has the hallmarks Lynch looked for in a fast grower: a large, underpenetrated market, a replicable product suite, and a management team that has been compounding book value and earnings consistently for nearly a decade. A forward P/E of 12.96x for a business likely to grow earnings 30-40% in FY26 is almost embarrassingly cheap.

The leverage and cash flow picture requires vigilance — this is not a business to own and forget. Finance costs growing faster than revenue is the single biggest metric to track quarter-over-quarter; if NIMs compress below 6%, the growth story gets complicated. But at current valuations, the risk/reward strongly favors ownership. If Capri Global sustains 25%+ net profit growth for three more years — entirely plausible given the AUM trajectory — this could be a 3-4x from here.
